embeds.title: Previously reported papers (still in the 30-day window)

fields.name: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
fields.value: Tencent — The paper argues that autoregressive video diffusion models trained with teacher forcing can produce plausible continuations without actually learning how scenes evolve, because strong local visual continuity gives a shortcut for denoising the current chunk.

fields.name: LiveAct: Towards Real-Time Multi-Agent World Models with Heterogeneous Action Interfaces
fields.value: Kuaishou Technology — The paper studies multi-agent interactive video world models that generate one joint visual future for several independently controlled agents, which may take heterogeneous controls ranging from game buttons to continuous robot commands.

fields.name: JointLight: Human-Centric Video Relighting with Asynchronous RGB-Irradiance Joint Modeling
fields.value: Kuaishou Technology — The paper addresses precise illumination control in human-centric video relighting, noting that diffusion-based relighting methods either model light transport implicitly (hurting controllability) or use path-traced irradiance cues directly as control signals (introducing artifacts).

fields.name: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion
fields.value: NVIDIA — The paper addresses camera ego-motion drift over long horizons in diffusion-based video generation models.

fields.name: Agentic World Action Models
fields.value: NVIDIA; Dantong Niu is 1,2) — The paper introduces AW-0, an "agentic world action model" that jointly generates code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled streams in one mixture-of-transformers architecture.

fields.name: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models
fields.value: Google — The paper argues that a world model's visual foundation should combine physical-state information, language alignment, and pixel reconstruction in one representation.

fields.name: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
fields.value: NVIDIA; this affiliation is confirmed directly from the primary source (the paper's own affiliation block), not the pre-screen keyword hit, but the HTML rendering does not map any specific named author to NVIDIA individually. — As interactive streaming video generation advances, there has been no unified way to evaluate real-time interaction with generated video.

fields.name: SceneRig: An Agentic System for Simulation-Ready 3D Scene Reconstruction from Single Images
fields.value: Luma AI; it is a well-known applied-AI company for generative 3D/video (Genie, Dream Machine/Ray2). Kept per the skill's "when unsure, flag rather than drop" rule, for a human to judge. — Simulation is valuable for robotics, but building diverse, simulation-ready 3D scenes at scale is difficult, and single-image reconstruction alone does not guarantee objects are correctly identified, placed, and physically grounded.

fields.name: Pair-Free Coarse-to-Real Video Generation via Real-to-Coarse Image Supervision
fields.value: Roblox and Adobe; the arXiv HTML markup lists these four institutions together in one note without marking which exact author maps to which, though a footnote confirms at least one author did "work done while at Roblox" — The paper addresses coarse-to-real (C2R) video generation — converting coarse animation, simulation, or game-rendered video into photorealistic video while preserving scene layout, camera motion, and dynamics — without needing expensive aligned (coarse, realistic) video pairs.

fields.name: OverSeer: Multi-Agent World Models Beyond What Agents See
fields.value: Meta; Chen is listed with University of Oxford only — Video world models are hard to extend to multiple agents because each agent needs its own video stream, and those streams must stay consistent over time and with each other.

fields.name: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
fields.value: SkyworkAI — Matrix-Game 4.0 separates game execution from visual generation via an "executable game harness": a lightweight game engine holds persistent world state and interaction rules, a multimodal coding agent turns player ideas into game code and dynamic scene captions, and an autoregressive-video-model re

fields.name: Latent Bridge: From Video Latents to 3D Geometry via Feature Alignment
fields.value: Horizon Robotics; it is a Chinese autonomous-driving/robotics AI chip and software company (publicly listed), kept here per the skill's "when unsure, flag rather than drop" rule for a human to judge as a possibly comparable industry lab. — Video generation and feed-forward 3D reconstruction normally use separate representations, requiring RGB decoding and re-encoding to recover geometry from generated video latents.

fields.name: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
fields.value: NVIDIA; several also hold secondary academic affiliations (Technion; Bar-Ilan University — Video generation models produce realistic motion, but that motion stays in pixels and cannot easily be reused as replayable 3D animation in a 3D scene.

fields.name: GALA: Geometry-Aware Language Model for Controllable Object Arrangement
fields.value: Tencent — GALA is a geometry-aware language model that predicts the 6D pose of one target object at a time for controllable 3D object arrangement, using explicit point-cloud perception instead of oriented-bounding-box (OBB) approximations.
